newsitem.title: INDIA: German minister speaks of defence cuts.
newsitem.headline: German minister speaks of defence cuts.

text.p: German Defence Minister Volker Ruehe said on Thursday military budget cuts had forced Bonn to cancel a proposed missile deal with France.

But the German defence ministry in Bonn denied that it would cut the number of Eurofighter combat aircraft it plans to buy, and said it had only pulled out of buying one version of the French-made Apache air-launched cruise missile.
"We don't have the money for that," Ruehe told a news conference in New Delhi when asked if Germany had called off talks with France to buy the Apache for its Tornado combat jets.
"Everybody has budget cuts," Ruehe said. "France has, Great Britain, Germany has. We are in a difficult decision-making process."
Ruehe, speaking at the end of a two-day visit to India, the first by a German defence minister, said negotiations over the Eurofighter were continuing.

"Especially the question of money we can use for the Eurofighter in the next four years... I will negotiate until I have satisfactory results. I can only spend the money I have. We need a plane and we want it to be a European plane," he said.
A Bonn defence ministry spokesman said Germany still intended to buy 180 Eurofighters -- 140 fighters and 40 fighter-bombers -- which are to be built by a four-country European consortium.
Ruehe was earlier quoted by Reuters telling reporters in New Delhi that Germany would cut back its Eurofighter order to 140.
The spokesman also said Germany had not abandoned plans to buy the Apache missile. But talks on buying one model -- the air-launched MAG Apache 1.1 anti-runway model -- had stopped, he added.
"The development of the Apache is continuing, but no numbers have yet been named," the spokesman said, without giving further details. Lagardere's Matra unit is the main contractor on Apache.
Germany's defence budget is under pressure from planned government spending cuts next year and the impact of a sluggish economy on state revenues.
No decision has yet been announced on buying Eurofighters, and talks are continuing with the aircraft's makers on how to finance serial production of a total of over 600 aircraft.
The Eurofighter is due to be built by a consortium linking Daimler Benz unit Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (Dasa) with British Aerospace Plc, Alenia SpA of Italy and Spain's CASA.
